status: Local bounded disposed-sandbox reclamation candidate passed the complete native gate, exact archive binding proof and actual installed Minutei SDK 0.9.0 interoperability. Not deployed or published.
candidateIdentity: A new unpublished candidate with distinct archive hashes; the previously deployed 0.10.0 archive is not overwritten.

contracts.action: vm.reclaim with limit 1..1000; only manage; root must already be disposed
contracts.progress: pending, blocked with nonterminal process IDs, or complete for the observed sweep; removed counts acknowledged deletion targets in that call
contracts.persistence: reclamations/<id>.json stores the phase and a fresh random publication revision under conditional R2 writes
contracts.retained: A disposed head with a native Rust empty manifest, cleared environment and its original control policy/creation metadata; a small progress object. ID reuse remains forbidden.
contracts.renewal: Only the administrator can issue fresh manage-only tokens for a disposed root. New non-management grants are forbidden.
contracts.continuation: Each call reads current state and deletes a leading bounded page. A later call after complete starts another sweep. A native cursor is used only within a call when a retained head is the sole item in a truncated object page.

verified: Live-root rejection, invalid limit rejection and denial without management permission before progress creation.
Native bulk removal of 1000 objects with 1005 seeded content objects plus actual file/code/output and other scoped data.
Limit-one batches, a retained head inside the object prefix, and no neighboring sandbox deletion.
Worker replacement between batches resumes persisted progress and completes.
The Rust empty manifest replaces the disposed filesystem graph and its environment is cleared. The same ID still cannot be recreated.
Queued receipts block collection without deletion or receipt mutation until actual native Queue disposal settlement.
A queued receipt reappearing during a later data phase blocks deletion; native settlement allows collection to resume.
Delivery replay after receipt deletion is acknowledged without recreating execution state.
Fresh management-only authority can collect a late orphan after a completed sweep. Read authority is not restored.
Three concurrent collection requests produce accepted progress or declared 409 conflicts; a subsequent sweep reaches persisted completion.
The exact archived SDK compiles its consumer and reaches reclamation completion through a native Worker service binding.

nativeReferenceScope: The installed binding contracts and native tests govern implementation. The provider reference confirms a 1000-key deletion maximum, partial list pages, conditional writes and strongly consistent deletes.

delivery.backend: Not deployed; the existing production Worker still runs the previously recorded published-software candidate.
delivery.publication: No GitHub authentication or package/repository publication.
delivery.minutei: The installed client and actual application fixtures remain unchanged at the recorded commit. The new collection action is not exercised by the 0.9.0 consumer; its existing Code Mode/tenant flows are compatibility checks.

limits: Collection is explicit and removes retained private receipts/output; disposal alone still retains them. No automatic retention timer or background collector is installed.
This is not a cross-object write fence. An earlier request can leave a late orphan; another sweep is required.
Nonterminal orphaned inline receipts without a recovery deadline remain blocked pending process-lifecycle repair. The collector never invents terminal settlement.
Automatic crash recovery, live-sandbox block collection and production performance/cost remain open.
The actual remote Minutei application/authentication/model path and history Queue consumption are not verified. The native consumer fixture intentionally has no history consumer.
The earlier remote preview 1101 remains an unresolved observation in persistent-binding-production.json.
Full AgentOS parity remains open in docs/parity.md.
